notes.meaning: John sees a sparkling river flowing directly from the throne shared by God and the Lamb. This living water pictures the pure, eternal life and refreshment that God gives His people, often seen as the work of the Holy Spirit. Eden once had a river, but this heavenly river never runs dry.

Along the river and throughout the city stands the tree of life, bearing twelve fresh harvests of fruit each year. In Eden, humans were cut off from this tree after falling into sin, but here God restores access to it in unending abundance. Its leaves bring perpetual health and peace to all the nations of the redeemed.

Every trace of the ancient curse brought on the world by sin is completely gone. God and the Lamb sit on the throne in the middle of the city, and His people actively worship and serve Him. In this holy place, nothing ruined or rebellious will ever exist again.

God's people will look straight into His face and see His glory without fear. His name will be openly marked on their foreheads, showing that they belong completely to Him and reflect His holy character.
Night and darkness are wiped away forever, so there is no need for sun or lamps. The Lord God Himself will be the direct light of His people, and they will share in His eternal royal rule forever.

An angel confirms that everything shown in these visions is completely reliable and true. The same God who guided the spirits of the ancient prophets sent His angel to show His servants the events that must soon happen.
Jesus promises that He is coming soon to bring history to its finish. A special blessing rests on everyone who takes this prophecy to heart and faithfully obeys its words.
John confirms with his own name that he really heard and saw all these marvelous visions. Overcome with deep awe and gratitude, he falls down to worship at the feet of the guiding angel.

The angel immediately stops John and refuses to be worshipped. He explains that he is merely a fellow servant alongside John, the prophets, and all who obey God's word, commanding John to worship God alone.

Unlike the prophet Daniel, who was told to seal up his vision for a distant future, John is told to keep this prophecy open. The time of its fulfillment is near, and God's people need its warnings and comforts right away.

This solemn warning shows that human choices will soon be fixed forever. Those who stubbornly choose evil and impurity will stay that way, while those who follow God will continue in righteousness and holiness.
Jesus repeats His promise that He is coming soon, bringing the final judgment with Him. He will reward and repay every person according to what they have actually done.

Jesus declares that He is the Alpha and the Omega, the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet. As the beginning and the end of all things, He has the authority of God Himself to create, guide, and judge the world.

Blessed are those who wash their robes clean by trusting in Christ. Because of His saving work, they receive the joyful right to eat from the tree of life and walk through the gates into the holy city.

Outside the safety of the holy city are all who remain filthy and unrepentant. This list includes people who practice magic arts, sexual immorality, murder, idolatry, and habitual lying, none of whom can enter God's pure kingdom.

Jesus personally speaks to assure the churches that this whole message comes straight from Him. He calls Himself both the root and descendant of King David—showing He is both David's Lord as God and his royal Son as man—and the bright morning star that brings in the eternal day.

The Holy Spirit and the church together cry out for the Lord Jesus to return. At the same time, this invitation calls anyone who is spiritually thirsty to come to Christ and drink freely of the water of life without cost.

differ.view: This verse proves that Jesus died for every single person and offers salvation freely to anyone who chooses to believe.
This free gospel offer to all who thirst flows from God's eternal decree to redeem His chosen people.

notes.meaning: A strict warning is spoken to anyone who hears the words of this prophecy. If anyone deliberately adds anything to what God has spoken, God will add to that person the terrible plagues described in this book.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: This verse warns only against altering the text of John's vision in Revelation, rather than ruling out sacred tradition or teachings outside the Bible.

notes.meaning: In the same way, anyone who cuts away or rejects the words of this prophecy faces severe judgment. God will take away that person's share in the tree of life and in the holy city.

differ.view: True believers cannot lose their salvation; this warning applies to people who only claimed to belong to Christ or seemed to have a share.

notes.meaning: Jesus gives His final word of assurance that He is truly coming soon. John eagerly responds on behalf of all believers with the prayer, 'Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!'
The book closes with a warm blessing wishing the undeserved favor of the Lord Jesus to be with all His people. Grace is the foundation of Christian hope from beginning to end.
